text: Planting timing (ពេលវេលាដាំដុះ) and spacing (ចម្ងាយដាំ / គម្លាតដាំ) should be decided from rainfall, soil moisture, water availability, and crop variety -- not a fixed calendar date. Cambodia's wet season runs roughly May-October and dry season roughly November-April, but actual rainfall onset and end vary year to year, and Preah Vihear farmers are experiencing increasingly unpredictable rainfall and temperatures. For rain-fed rice (ស្រូវពឹងទឹកភ្លៀង), which dominates much of the province, planting should be coordinated with reliable onset of the rainy season rather than a set date: planting too early into dry soil risks the crop with no follow-up water, while planting too late risks sensitive growth stages falling outside the useful rainy period. For vegetables, dry-season production can work where irrigation is available, but a farmer without dependable water should not be pushed into a water-demanding crop just because prices look favorable. Spacing is crop- and variety-specific: rice may use broadcasting, transplanting, or direct row seeding; cassava is planted from stem cuttings (មែកពូជ/ដើមពូជ); cashew is a perennial tree needing much wider spacing; vegetable spacing depends on the crop and whether it's direct-seeded or transplanted. Do not give one universal spacing number -- it depends on crop, variety, soil fertility, water, and production system. For small plots, test a new planting date or spacing on a small trial area first. The safest framing for the chatbot: 'For rain-fed rice, plant when adequate soil moisture has been established and the expected rainy period is sufficient for the selected variety to complete its critical growth stages; adjust for local rainfall conditions rather than a fixed date.'
